$comment: Inventory of every third-party binary physically redistributed inside a linq2db artifact.
Read Build/licenses/README.md before editing. Regenerate the notices after any change:
To find out what changed after a dependency bump, run -Action harvest.

components.displayName: IBM Data Server Driver for ODBC and CLI (clidriver)
components.license: IBM International Program License Agreement - Redistributables
components.notes: IBM grants redistribution of the Redistributables in object-code form only as part of a value-added application developed using the Program. linq2db satisfies all three limbs: the client is bundled inside linq2db scaffolding packages and the LINQPad driver rather than offered standalone, those packages are our own application built using the client, and only compiled assemblies and native libraries are shipped - no IBM source. Note on scope: IBM ships its own enumeration at clidriver/license/odbc_REDIST.txt, reproduced below. Of the 86 distinct clidriver binaries shipped here, 34 do not appear on that list - 30 GSKit crypto libraries (gsk8*.dll), 2 ICC crypto libraries (icclib084/085.dll) and Microsoft Visual C++ 12.0 runtime (msvcp120.dll, msvcr120.dll). All of them are delivered inside IBM own NuGet package as runtime dependencies of the driver (GSKit provides its TLS support), so the list reads as incomplete rather than exclusive.

components.license: Microsoft Software License Terms - Microsoft System CLR Types for Microsoft SQL Server 2022
components.notes: The bundled binary is version 170.1000.7, whose embedded license.md is the MICROSOFT SQL SERVER VNEXT COMMUNITY PREVIEW pre-release text: its term ended 09/30/2022, it grants installation "solely to internally evaluate it and provide feedback to Microsoft", and it contains no DISTRIBUTABLE CODE section or any distribution grant. That appears to be a packaging error on a stable release - 160.1000.6 of the same package carries ordinary MICROSOFT SOFTWARE LICENSE TERMS for MICROSOFT SYSTEM CLR TYPES FOR MICROSOFT SQL SERVER 2022, with an explicit DISTRIBUTABLE CODE grant covering third-party distribution. Reported to Microsoft. The terms reproduced here are the 160.1000.6 ones, which is what we understand to have been intended for this package; the text Microsoft actually attached to 170.1000.7 is the pre-release one described above.
components.revisit: Drop the licence substitution once Microsoft ships a 170.x package carrying corrected terms: replace texts/microsoft-sqlserver-types-license.md with that package own license.md and clear this marker. Reported to Microsoft; tracked on issue #5731.

components.license: SAP Developer License Agreement 3.2 (see notes - provenance is not certain for this build)
components.notes: Sap.Data.Hana.v4.5.dll is checked into Redist/SapHana and copied into the T4 tools folder; no licence accompanied that copy in this repository. The text reproduced here is the SAP Developer License Agreement 3.2, which SAP attaches to the HANA .NET providers it publishes on nuget.org (Sap.Data.Hana.Net.v6.0/v8.0/v10.0) - it is the best available statement of SAP terms for this provider, but it is not necessarily the agreement under which the .NET Framework copy here was obtained, which came from a HANA client installation. Read it before relying on this component: section 1 grants a non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence and section 2(a) states the software may not be provided or made available to any third party. Note also that only the managed assembly is packed, not the native libadonetHDB it calls into, so it cannot connect unless the SAP HANA client is already installed.
components.revisit: Redistribution of Sap.Data.Hana.v4.5.dll is unresolved and needs a decision: either establish terms that permit it, or stop packing it from linq2db.SapHana and linq2db.t4models. Tracked on issue #5862.

components.license: Microsoft Software License Terms - Microsoft SQL Server Compact 4.0 SP1
components.notes: Terms sourced from SQLCE_EULA_ENU.rtf as shipped in the Microsoft.SqlServer.Compact 4.0.8876.1 package; the copy here is a plain-text rendering of that RTF, which is also published at http://www.microsoft.com/web/webpi/eula/SQLCE_SP1_EULA_ENU.rtf. Section 2a grants Distributable Code rights - "you are permitted to distribute in programs you develop", "You may copy and distribute the object code form of code listed in REDIST.TXT files" and "Third Party Distribution" - subject to adding significant primary functionality, which linq2db scaffolding does. The binaries in Redist/SqlCe are byte-identical to that package's contents (verified by SHA-256 on System.Data.SqlServerCe.dll, sqlceca40.dll x86 and amd64, sqlcese40.dll and msvcr90.dll); sourcing them from the package instead is tracked on issue #5861.
